layout: Use case: sketch-to-render. Create a fleshed-out interior concept sheet based ONLY on the upper-right general store drawing in the supplied sketch. Ignore the bowling alley on the left and house at bottom-right. Preserve the sketch's spatial idea: a friendly small quadrupedal pony shopkeeper behind a low wooden checkout counter on the left/back-left, three stocked horizontal shelves across the back wall, a substantial freestanding wooden merchandise shelf on the right, a basket/barrel display near the left foreground, and a generous open middle aisle. Expand into a coherent cozy pony-town general store, with useful everyday goods: jars of preserves, paper sacks of oats/flour, folded cloth, baskets of apples and carrots, small earthenware pots. No human cashier, no modern supermarket, no bowing/bowling elements. Deliver one landscape art-director concept sheet: dominant clean 3/4 interior perspective showing the whole shop; smaller clear top-down floor plan inset with entrance at front and circulation around the central space. Warm pencil/ink linework with restrained watercolor colors; this is the developed design stage, readable architectural forms and furniture, not photorealistic. The pony is only a scale/occupancy reference. Keep the room compact, approximately 8m wide by 7m deep with a 3.4m ceiling, rounded timber posts and cozy plaster walls. Make the furniture actually constructible and the aisles wide enough for a human VR player and ponies. Do not include house/bowling floor plans. Avoid long annotation text; no branding or watermark.
game_style: Use case: style-transfer / stylized-concept. Input image is the accepted layout reference for a pony-town general store, not a texture to paste onto geometry. Create the second, game-art concept stage: turn the same shop into a believable real-time 3D interior for Home: Equestria, a My Little Pony inspired first-person VR game. Its art direction is stylized cartoon geometry with realistic warm light, flat-ish albedo, very thin understated outlines, clear bold silhouettes rather than painterly micro-detail. Preserve the arrangement: checkout on left/back-left, stocked shelves along back, long tall freestanding shelving to right, apples/carrots in low barrels left foreground, open center circulation and green woven rug, front entrance. Replace the generic rustic brown-on-brown realism with cozy Equestrian character: soft cream plaster, chunky rounded warm honey-wood beams, subtle muted sage and dusty mauve trim, slightly bowed shelf edges, scalloped small wood brackets, gentle hoof-friendly proportions. Goods are bold low-poly readable jars, sacks, folded cloth, baskets, pottery. Counter 0.95m high, ceiling 3.4m; room 8x7m. Human walk clearance alongside pony-height furniture. Light softly through a right side window; restrained warm lanterns, no excessive bloom or fog. Grounded PBR-style material response, no hard cel lighting bands. Main image: wide eye-level in-engine-quality 3D perspective from entrance, facing back wall. Include a small secondary orthographic top-down layout and a few matching modular furniture views along bottom. Keep the architecture consistent between views. No need to include the shopkeeper in this pass: interior geometry is the deliverable. No labels/brand names or modern retail tech. No exterior, no bowling alley, no house, no photoreal wood grain or densely engraved ornament. This image will be used to build actual 3D meshes, so show complete plausible supported furniture and practical aisle geometry.
